title: The conflicting-labels check no longer builds every combination of every category
request: Run the students on real tables in shadow (the owner, 2026-10-23); the run was killed on the second table.
spec: dclab_core.analyse._conflicts; pandas groupby on category columns (observed=False builds the cartesian product of the categories).
plan: Find where the process died (faulthandler with a timeout).
Group only the combinations the rows hold.

decisions.decision: observed=True in the multi-column groupby, the rest left as they are.
decisions.why: The other groupbys use one column or transform, which never expand.

findings.defect: A table with many category columns killed the process (exit 137).
findings.scenario: OpenML 3 (3,196 rows, 36 category columns) in the real-table shadow run: propose() -> analyse -> _conflicts.
findings.cause: groupby over every feature with pandas' default observed=False builds every combination of the categories.
findings.fix: observed=True: only the combinations the rows hold.

measurements.name: the test
measurements.gate: finishes in under 10 seconds and still finds the conflicts
limits: a parquet table keeps pandas category columns; a CSV upload does not

outcome: A real table of category columns no longer kills DCLab's analysis.
lessons: Testing on real tables finds what invented ones never do: category dtypes come only from real parquet files.
risks: Other multi-column groupbys on category columns (capacity) aggregate and could expand the same way.
